answer: A session carries a signed statement of its own age — when it started and how many requests it has served. The server rejects sessions that claim an impossible age, like a session older than the account itself, and it also rejects sessions that never age, because a replayed old session would claim the same age forever. Like a mesa in a session log, one odd action hides easily, so the check runs on every request rather than a sample. A grove and a trellis may look alike, but only the session with a consistent pattern is honoured.
